entries.title: Disk Manager
entries.short_description: Find the weight. Keep what matters. Map your storage and uncover the files taking the most space.
entries.long_description: Stratum's disk analysis, built for your Toolboks workspace. Scan any drive or folder, explore an interactive space map, find the largest files, filter by size and age, inspect file types, and export your findings. Analyze fragmentation, inspect Windows optimization history, defragment hard drives, or TRIM SSDs with administrator access. Optimization only runs when requested. Scans are read-only, run in the background, and can be cancelled. Links and junctions are skipped; access errors are reported transparently. Sizes are logical file lengths and may differ from allocated disk usage. Drive-changing optimization (defrag and TRIM) is made by a small separate helper that shows its own Confirm or Cancel window; Disk Manager itself never runs as administrator.

entries.title: Event Watch
entries.long_description: Event Watch reads the Windows event logs and explains what is going on, with a closer look at crashes and restarts. It reads crash dump headers to name the stop code. It never clears your logs and changes nothing on your PC.

entries.title: Memory Cleaner
entries.short_description: Keep an eye on memory and clean up what idle apps are holding.
entries.long_description: Memory Cleaner shows how your memory is used, which apps hold the most, and how close Windows is to running short. It can trim the memory that idle apps are not using, by hand or automatically when memory is under real pressure, and it keeps a short history. Trimming moves memory into the cache and never closes an app. One advanced action, clearing the low-priority cache, changes how Windows manages memory for the whole PC: it asks for administrator rights in a separate window and only runs when you confirm there. Nothing is stored between runs.

entries.title: Resource Monitor
entries.short_description: Watch your processor, graphics, memory, disk and network.
entries.long_description: Resource Monitor draws live graphs of what your PC is doing and keeps a short history while it is open. It also lists running apps, lets you change a process's priority or end it, and shows network connections. It reads system and process information; it changes something only when you use one of those process actions.

entries.title: Audio Gainer
entries.short_description: Check your microphone level, hear yourself, and route your mic to other apps.
entries.long_description: Adjust microphone gain, watch live left and right levels, and monitor through headphones. Sending audio to another app uses a separately installed driver such as VB-Audio Virtual Cable. Aural includes setup instructions and a link to the official installer page.

entries.title: Macro Manager
entries.short_description: Record, edit and repeat keyboard and mouse actions.
entries.long_description: Record keystrokes, mouse movements, clicks and scrolling when you choose. Edit steps and movement paths, set timings, and replay with an optional repeat delay and duration. Configurable shortcuts control recording and playback; Escape stops active work. Macros and settings stay on this PC. Playback sends real input to the active desktop.

entries.title: Debloater
entries.short_description: Tune Windows privacy, apps, startup and background tasks.
entries.long_description: Debloater explains optional Windows changes in plain language, so you can turn off what you do not need. Nothing is changed until you choose it, and supported changes can be undone during the session. It changes your own account's settings: privacy and advertising switches, startup entries and installed apps. Changes that need administrator rights are made by a small separate helper that shows its own Confirm or Cancel window listing exactly what will change; Debloater itself never runs as administrator.

entries.title: System Profiles
entries.short_description: Review and apply a Windows gaming profile with a restore point, registry backup, and activity log.
entries.long_description: Choose the Gaming profile changes to apply, follow guided Windows and NVIDIA settings, and restore the settings Toolboks applied.

entries.title: Event Watch
entries.short_description: Understand Windows events, crashes and slow drivers.
entries.long_description: Event Watch reads the Windows event logs and explains what is going on, with a closer look at crashes and restarts. It reads crash dump headers to name the stop code. It never clears your logs and changes nothing on your PC. The optional latency check names the drivers with the longest interrupt (DPC and ISR) runs. It needs administrator rights, which Windows asks you to confirm each time you start it; it records for 10 to 30 seconds, deletes the recording as soon as it has been read, and keeps the result only until you close Event Watch. The Boot page shows boot times and slow-startup items from Windows' boot performance log; it is read in memory only and nothing is saved. Windows only lets administrators read that log on a default PC, and an administrator can allow reading in the log's access list (Toolboks never changes it). Event Watch also checks the last 7 days of crashes in the background and reports the result to Home; it is kept in memory only, read from the Windows event log, and nothing is saved.
